back: A ledger account that brings together the cost, accumulated depreciation and proceeds of an asset sold; its balance is the profit or loss on disposal.
Proceeds − carrying amount at the date of disposal.
Cost of the asset sold; a profit as the balancing figure.
Accumulated depreciation on that asset; proceeds (bank, buyer or part-exchange allowance); a loss as the balancing figure.
Dr new asset with the allowance, Cr disposal; Dr new asset with the cash paid, Cr bank. The new asset is at full cost.

front: What does a profit on disposal mean?
back: Earlier depreciation was too high (carrying amount below the proceeds). A loss means it was too low.
Dr buyer's account (receivable), Cr disposal. Bank is debited when the buyer pays.
Profit: other income. Loss: expense. Neither is in revenue or cost of sales.
Only the accumulated depreciation on the asset sold, up to the date of sale as the policy requires.
